newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA's profits jump 27 percent on strong sales.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA's profits jump 27 percent on strong sales.

text.p: CompUSA Inc. said Wednesday its profits jumped by 27 percent in the fourth quarter of last year to a record $23.7 million as it posted strong sales gains in the important holiday shopping period.

The retailer of personal computers and related products said net income in its fiscal 1997 second quarter, which ended Dec. 28, climbed to $23.7 million, or 25 cents a share, from $18.7 million, or 20 cents a share, a year ago.
It added that sales increased 22 percent to $1.2 billion from $983 million, although sales at the 95 stores open at least one year grew by only 1.5 percent.
"Overall, we are pleased with our financial results for the second quarter," Chief Executive James Halpin said in a statement.

"CompUSA achieved record earnings despite the highly promotional environment during the holidays and slowdown in retail sales toward the end of the season. We believe these results demonstrate the strength of CompUSA's unique operating model and the dedication of our team members."
CompUSA now operates 122 "superstores" in 55 major metropolitan markets throughout the United States. It also owns PCs Compleat Inc., a leading direct reseller of personal computers and peripherals.
The company said net income for the six months rose to $38.3 million, or 40 cents a share, from $25 million, or 28 cents a share.
Sales for the six months rose by 24 percent to a record $2.19 billion from $1.77 billion, with sales at the 95 stores open one year or more expanding by 4.1 percent.
CompUSA's stock gained 37.5 cents to $17.625 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
